angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 615,695 km at 172.03 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.8129 +/- 0.0197 mas (same row, RUWE 0.98): 172.03 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.885 +/- 0.046 solar radii from Turner et al. 2019, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-177 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.485.5790T/abstract): 615,695 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.876 +/- 0.038 solar masses from Turner et al. 2019, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-177 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.485.5790T/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5017 +/- 70 K from Turner et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-177 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.485.5790T/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Turner et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-177 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.485.5790T/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-177.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.487, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
